explicitimplicitwell-posednessalways single-valuedmay be multi-valued or have no solution / output only closest point to the variety
So the two projects take opposite positions on the same question. El Ghaoui et al. engineer
away multi-valuedness because it obstructs a prediction rule. Lenticulum keeps it, because
a relation that branches is still a relation — and the branch locus has a name and a theory
(Branches and the Discriminant), and energy minimisation is total precisely where
root-finding is not (Implicit Learners §“The claim”).
That is the full scope the title does not reach: not a criticism of the paper, but a statement
of where its assumptions place it on the table in §1.
4. On Learning in Implicit Generative Models (1610.03483)
Mohamed & Lakshminarayanan’s sense is (1), and it is the sharpest of the three because it is
about what you can compute rather than about how the model is written:

A model is implicit if it defines a sampling procedure and not a density.

Their consequence is the interesting part, and it is worked through in
Implicit Generative Models: without a likelihood you cannot do maximum likelihood, so you
must learn by comparison — estimate a density ratio or difference between p^\ast and
q_\theta and drive it to one. GANs are one of four ways to do that.
Note what this shares with sense (3) and what it does not. Both give up a closed-form
objective. But an implicit generative model gives up the density while keeping the
direction; an implicit learner gives up the direction while (often) keeping a
perfectly computable residual. LinearConstraintFactor has an entirely tractable density and
no preferred direction; a GAN generator is the exact opposite.
5. Why this matters for the vault
Implicit Learners lists three model families — algebraic, equilibrium, diffusion — and
each is implicit in sense (3). The adversarial family added by lib/Adversarial.jl is not:
it is sense (1), and all three of its factors are unidirectional.
So the honest structure is two-dimensional, and the vault had been treating it as one:

sense (3) is what makes a factor worth having a Polarity at all, and what
Mycelium.jl exists to schedule;
sense (1) is what makes a belief a SampleBelief rather than a parametric one, and it
is what breaks Mycelium.combine.

A model can be either, both, or neither, and the two failures land in different parts of the
codebase.
Related: Implicit Learners, Implicit Generative Models, GANs as Two Factors,
DEQ as a Relation, The Equilibrium Family, Channels and Polarity,
Branches and the Discriminant, The Structural Gap to ModelingToolkit

Map-of-Content.title: Map of Content
Map-of-Content.content:
overview

Every note of the Lenticulum vault, in reading order. How the vault is organised and what
its conventions are: Start Here. The general category theory — Para, lenses, Markov
categories, Bayesian lenses, statistical games — is in the
CT-ML wiki; links to it below are ordinary
web links, links within this vault are wikilinks.

Three papers are the backbone, and one bridge layer connects them to Julia:

Categorical Foundations of Gradient-Based Learning
(Cruttwell, Gavranović, Ghani, Wilson, Zanasi) — how ordinary deep learning is a
parametric lens. This is the theory Lux.jl already implements without saying so.
AutoBayes (St Clere Smithe & Perin) — how
Bayesian inference is a statistical game, which is a parametric lens whose
backward pass is a posterior rather than a gradient. This is what Lenticulum.jl
implements.
A Tutorial on Energy-Based Learning
(LeCun, Chopra, Hadsell, Ranzato, Huang) — how learning works with no normalisation at
all: an energy, an argmin, and a factor graph. Read after the other two, but it is the
layer README’s own table was written from, and the one most of the implementation
actually runs in.

Read in this order.
References: Bibliography, every work cited in the vault, the implementation notes and the
tutorials, generated from one .bib file that the documentation also uses.
1. The classical story (what Lux.jl is)

Para — parameters as a categorical construction
Lens — forward/backward pairs, get and put
Parametric Lens — Definition 2.5, the object Lux layers really are
Cartesian Reverse Differential Category — where the gradient comes from
Learning Components as Parametric Lenses — model, loss, learning rate, optimiser
Lux as a Parametric Lens — the concrete Lux.jl ↔ lens dictionary

2. The Bayesian story (what Lenticulum.jl is)

Open Models and Latent Channels — Definitions 1–8: a kernel with an explicit latent
space, and how the DAG restriction is lifted
Composition of Open Models — Definitions 4–7
Inversions and Bayesian Lenses — Definitions 9–11: Bayes’ law as a chain rule, and the
inversion as a free choice
Composition of Bayesian Lenses — Definition 12, Theorem 13
Variational Free Energy — Definition 17, Proposition 18: the energy/entropy split
Factors are Parameterized Statistical Games — Definitions 20 and 27: the definition
Lenticulum factors satisfy, and what actually gets optimised
Composition of Statistical Games — Definition 22, Theorem 23 (the chain rule)
Composition of Gradients — Definitions 28–29, Remark 30: laxness
AutoBayes Examples as Factor Graphs — Appendix A, worked through

2b. The energy story (what is left when you stop normalising)
LeCun’s tutorial and the modern EBM literature. Structurally below AutoBayes: drop the
partition function and a statistical game becomes an energy-based factor graph.
Read Energies and Entropies first: the seven things this vault calls “energy” and the
five it calls “entropy”, side by side, with the confusions they invite.

Energy-Based Learning — the framework; why README’s table is this paper’s table;
loss functionals, the concept Lenticulum has no slot for; and the collapse problem,
which gaussian.jl already guards against under the name complexity
Energy-Based Factor Graphs — LeCun §6 is Mycelium without the beliefs. min-sum is
the T\to0 limit of sum-product, so a DiracBelief message is a min-sum message and
three packages’ “missing entropy” is the Bethe form degenerating correctly
Training Energy-Based Models — Song & Kingma, Du & Mordatch. Two of the three standard
EBM training methods are already implemented here under other names: score matching is
VariationalDiffusion, NCE is Adversarial.RatioFactor — and NCE with a known noise
distribution is the belief_logdensity messages §1 has always wanted

2c. Types
What kind of type theory this is, and what the code’s own types are doing.

Probabilistic Types — “probabilistic type” names three different things. Beliefs are
not the probability monad (the merge operation is not monadic), but
r_\theta \approx 0 is a graded type judgment with the energy as its grade — and the
grade lives in a semiring, which is the temperature
The Type Discipline of a Factor Graph — a factor graph is neither linear nor cartesian
but Frobenius; putting polarity in the type domain already caught a real bug; and five
separately-recorded gaps turn out to be one typing problem

3. The bridge to Lenticulum.jl

Channels and Polarity — reconciling AutoBayes’ X/⟦c⟧/Y with the README’s
P_{in} + P_{out} + P_{latent} = \mathrm{Id}
Scalar and Multivariate Energy — the design decision that is ours, not the
paper’s: two energies, and the chain rule adapted to the multivariate one
Implicit Learners — the three model families, and why the multivariate energy
is what makes them work
AutoBayes to Lenticulum — the full naming dictionary paper → Julia
ModelingToolkit as an Acausal Relation — the other bridge: MTK is the implicit
column of README’s table minus the probability; Willems’ behaviors; why MTK’s
incidence graph is a factor graph, and why MTK solves where Mycelium propagates
Acausal Composition is a Hypergraph Category — how much structure it takes to wire an
arbitrary graph rather than a DAG; a variable node is a Frobenius spider, and improper
Gaussian beliefs are what make that work
The Structural Gap to ModelingToolkit — the question in the other direction: what
does MTK contain that Lenticulum does not? Five ranked items; two are not addable
Time as a Base — the design note: what an MTK × Lenticulum extension with a time
dimension would be. A base change, not a redesign — variables carry trajectories, and a
belief over a trajectory is a chain factor graph
Three Senses of Implicit — the word means three independent things: implicit
likelihood, implicit computation, implicit relation. Only the third buys you a polarity
Depth in Implicit Learning — is there a “no deep learning theorem”? Yes on the
linear-Gaussian fragment and no elsewhere — it is the d=1 case of a degree bound the
vault already derived; and depth-as-computation and depth-as-expressivity come apart
Prolog and Logic Programming — “the Prolog of machine learning”, scored honestly.
Modes are polarities exactly; Prolog is the boolean semiring of the same framework;
and the shortfall is one thing — schemas versus ground instances
Geometric Deep Learning and Physical Laws — equivariance constrains the map, a
law constrains the configuration; \dot x=-x is equivariant and conserves nothing.
The measured case: direct-force equivariant potentials are unstable in MD
(Bigi–Langer–Ceriotti, ICML 2025). And the converse — this project has no equivariance
The Table Revisited — the README’s table is an illustrating example (polynomials → varieties,
the one pair where every slot becomes a theorem), read row by row. Holds up; the one
real caveat is the Loss row collapses without a contrastive term; “symmetric” means
acausal; the whole table is the T\to0 limit of the AutoBayes layer

3b. The algebraic family, worked out
The first of the three Implicit Learners families in full detail — the case where every
abstract slot of the framework becomes computable, so the framework can be checked.
Entry point: Algebraic Implicit Learners.

model class: Varieties Ideals and Real Nullstellensatz, The Veronese Parametrisation,
Universal Approximation by Nash-Tognoli
learning: Fitting is a Nullspace Problem, The Parameter is a Grassmannian,
Algebraic versus Geometric Distance
inference: Inference as Root Finding, Branches and the Discriminant,
Backpropagation by the Implicit Function Theorem
structure: Composition is Elimination, Differential Algebra and DAE Factors,
Algebraic Statistics Bridge
first to build: Toric Models as Factors (exact discrete factors with known binomial
equations), Grassmann Mixing and Plücker Coordinates (a Plücker-feature alternative to
attention, and what it offers here); the plan is L-SPEC-004 Algebraic Factors Toric and Grassmannian
verdict: The Algebraic Factor as a Statistical Game,
Open Problems in Algebraic Implicit Learning
kernels: Kernel Methods for Implicit Learning — RBF and GP implicit surfaces, kernel PCA, density
ridges (the first tutorial’s model is a kernel density estimate), kernel exponential families
later: Symbolic Implicit Learning — relations as formulas found by search (noted, not built)

3c. Factor graphs and message passing
Mycelium.jl — how factors are wired and in what order they talk. The layer with no
counterpart in Lux.

Beliefs — what travels on an edge: Trivial Belief, Dirac Belief, Gaussian Belief,
Sample Belief, Categorical Belief, Mixture Belief, and how they pool (combine)
Belief Algebra — every other operation (addition, mixture, logic, projection, tempering) as a
factor whose messages are the operation; what exists, what is missing, what to build first
Factor Graphs — bipartite structure; the two acyclicity notions (istree vs isdag)
Everything is a Factor — data, priors, losses and optimisers as graph nodes, forced by Remark 24
Unusual Wirings — an output into a weight, an energy into an input, beliefs on weights and energies; risk measures as scalarisations
Messages are Inversions — a factor → variable message is c'_\pi; both exclusion principles
Polarity Resolution — target + available messages → a Polarity; the two legality checks
Schedules — the schedule zoo; tree exactness; pruning by edge direction
Bethe Free Energy — Theorem 23 generalised to graphs; energies add, entropies get a counting correction
Loopy Message Passing — what breaks off a tree, and the monodromy problem
Dynamic Graphs — adding and deleting factors while the graph runs (SLAM); the Bethe free
energy as the criterion; edges of a diffusion factor as noise levels
The Linear Gaussian Chain — the worked example: GTSAM’s OdometryExample, exact
marginals against the joint information matrix, and what this library is not

3d. The equilibrium family, worked out
The second of the three Implicit Learners families — SciML’s deep equilibrium networks
and neural ODEs, wrapped as factors. Entry point: The Equilibrium Family.

the fixed point: DEQ as a Relation — a DEQ is defined by a relation and shipped as a
function; the reverse solve; the contraction caveat made testable; why the IFT brings
automatic differentiation back
the flow: NeuralODE as an Invertible Factor — bidirectional for free, because a flow
is a diffeomorphism; the density correction, and why it is currently dead code

3e. The diffusion family, worked out
The third of the three Implicit Learners families — the case where the inversion is
neither exact nor a root-find but a proximal solve. Entry point:
The Diffusion Family.

the origin: ImplicitREDDiff — the founding note of the project: relations instead of
functions, input and output as masks chosen at inference time, and the energy the code computes
the forward process: The VP-SDE — Song et al. 2021; the perturbation kernel, the score
identity, Tweedie’s denoiser, and the tmin floor nobody documents
the inversion: RED-Diff as a Statistical Game — variational inference with a point-mass
posterior; the stop-gradient; and λ is derivable, not merely tunable
the factor: The Diffusion Factor — P_{in}+P_{out}+P_{latent}=\mathrm{Id} becomes a
Polarity; what a Dirac-valued message does to a factor graph
the implicit learner: Implicit Diffusion Learners — the stop-gradient field is the exact
gradient of a smoothed log-density; inference is a proximal point; the smoothing scale decides
the relation · Inference Signatures · Backpropagation through Implicit Inference — the
Lagrangian worked out, and a parabola learned from a circle by the adjoint alone ·
Deterministic Relaxation — a DEQ whose layer is the denoiser ·
The Implicit Diffusion Factor as a Statistical Game
composition: Composing Diffusion Factors — intersections of learned relations by adding
fields (a product of experts); conditioning as a special case; exactness at t > 0
expressiveness: Universal Approximation for Implicit Diffusion Learners — the answers of
any target with nondegenerate answers are reached, with an explicit constant; training,
consistency and branch points stay open
verdict: Open Problems in Implicit Diffusion Learning — theoretical problems (open or
intrinsic) separated from missing implementation, each with its evidence
alternatives: ProxDM and Proximal Alternatives — DPS, ΠGDM, ProxDM, plug-and-play, and
why RED-Diff was implemented first; ProxDM is now implemented (proxdm)
a conservative score: energy_network — the network outputs an energy, \varepsilon = \sigma_t\nabla E;
the learned relation gets a scalar energy, trained without nested AD in the loop
small networks, any AD backend: backends — Zygote, Enzyme, ForwardDiff or Reactant
through one field; a 5k-parameter MLP trained, inferred with and differentiated through

3f. The adversarial family, worked out
Implicit generative models — the case where what is missing is the density rather than
the direction, so every factor is unidirectional. Entry point:
Implicit Generative Models.

the paper: Implicit Generative Models — Mohamed & Lakshminarayanan; learning by
comparison; the four estimators; and why a density ratio is the answer to messages §1
the diagram: GANs as Two Factors — two parameter sets, three nodes, and one sign the
Bethe free energy cannot hold; the missing structure is an open game
the vocabulary: Three Senses of Implicit — filed under §3 above, and the reason this
family has no polarities

3g. Two-part architectures, and the meta-graph
Where GANs, reinforcement learning and control theory draw the same diagram — and what the
project would look like with factor graphs attached to the factor graph.

The Two-Part Diagram — the shared shape is the wiring, which is a trace and already
solved. What differs is the objective: one function (EM, VAE, active inference, LQG) fits
the Bethe free energy; minimax (GANs) and general bilevel (actor–critic) do not
The Inferencer and the Optimizer — the design note: meta-graphs over the base graph’s
messages and parameters. Half of it already exists as OptimiserFactor and
AmortisedInversion; it is loop-free because it is coordinate descent on one objective; and
it is the separation principle, exact for linear-Gaussian and failing into exploration

4. Implementation
Implementation notes live next to the code, per Start Here:
LenticulumCore.jl — LenticulumCore, abstract_types, channels, energy,
open_model, lens, statistical_game
Mycelium.jl — Mycelium, graph, polarity_resolution, messages,
schedules, passing, free_energy, factors
Lenticulum.jl — constraint, nonlinear, likelihood (beliefs.md and gaussian.md are not yet written)
VariationalDiffusion.jl — VariationalDiffusion, schedule, predictor,
reddiff, factor, analytic, implicit, implicit_factor, energy_network, proxdm, backends,
krylov, sampler, coverage
ImplicitLayers.jl — ImplicitLayers, solve, deq, flow, neuralode,
luxfactor
Adversarial.jl — Adversarial, generator, ratio
5. Project records
Decisions, problems and specifications, numbered so that notes, commits and issues can cite
them; the same layout as Moonkale’s and Sophia’s vaults.

Decisions — L-ADR-nnnn: what was chosen, by whom, and what follows. Among them
L-ADR-0002 Energies are vectors, scalarised late and
L-ADR-0003 Pointwise energy and free energy are separate levels
Problem Log — LP-nnn: what does not work yet and needs a decision, from GitHub issues
to gaps in the theory, e.g. LP-002 The Jacobian side is not implemented
Specifications — L-SPEC-nnn: contracts precise enough to test against, starting with
L-SPEC-001 The Factor Interface

6. Research questions
Open mathematical and statistical questions, each stated so that it can be worked on without
the rest of the vault: Research Questions (RQ-nnn). Among them
RQ-001 One Potential, Every Polarity (when one density answers every query direction) and
RQ-003 When Local Gradients Are Exact (the gradient terms AutoBayes drops).
Where this would be useful
Six domains with the same shape — a network of relations, sparse asynchronous observations,
some parts known and some fitted, and a residual that means something in the domain itself.

Motivating Examples — the overview, and the six properties they share
SLAM and Sensor Fusion · Trading and Financial Markets ·
Energy Markets and Power Grids
Metabolomics and Proteomics · Molecular Dynamics ·
Climate and Dynamical Systems
Language Models — a product of diffusion experts, not a mixture; why the framing
clarifies and the machinery does not
MNIST in Both Directions — (later) one model of (image, label): classify, draw, and
inpaint-and-classify by choosing ρ; the interfaces it needs first

Orientation

Related Julia Projects — where this sits in the Julia ecosystem, and when to use
something else. The nearest neighbour is RxInfer.jl; IncrementalInference.jl
has already solved the combine gap by kernel-density BP; and Catlab’s oapply is the
subgraph-as-factor operation the vault records as missing
RxInfer as a Backend — the nearest neighbour as an engine: gains for the probabilistic part,
five things a replacement would lose, and a connector with learned relations as RxInfer nodes
Sharing Types with RxInfer — (later) wrap ExponentialFamily types as beliefs instead of
converting; reuse RxInfer’s linearisation and unscented code for hand-written nonlinear factors
(NonlinearFactor now does both itself)
Backward Signatures — the backward pass at solver, factor and graph level: forward
arguments + forward result + cotangent; rrules on top (the solver’s is built); unrolled vs adjoint message passing
Why Julia — why not C++, Rust, PyTorch, JAX or Mojo: in Julia ordinary code is the compiled,
differentiable computation graph, with evidence from this repository and the costs stated
Parallelism and Compilation — parallelism, GPUs and XLA/MLIR in a dynamic SLAM
setting. There is no junction tree and no parallelism today; a sweep is quadratic in the
number of factors (measured); and the compile-vs-dynamic tension dissolves if you
compile the factor types, not the graph
Moonkale — a sister project in Rust: a graph-native
editor for code and notes, meant to become a diagram editor for these factor graphs (prototype;
the plan)
README — the pitch

Project/Decisions/Decisions.title: Decisions
Project/Decisions/Decisions.content:
overview

The decisions recorded for Lenticulum.jl, numbered L-ADR-nnnn; the L- keeps them apart from Moonkale’s ADRs and Sophia’s S-ADRs. A decision is proposed until Daniel accepts it. An accepted decision is not reopened without a new ADR that supersedes it. Use the ADR template (vault/templates/ADR Template.md) for a new one.

The log starts on 2026-10-22. Decisions taken before then and recorded retrospectively say so in their status line, and point to the notes where they were first written down. Longer design discussions stay in Design/; an ADR records the choice and links to them.

Project/Decisions/L-ADR-0001-Julia.title: L-ADR-0001 Julia
Project/Decisions/L-ADR-0001-Julia.content:
design

Status: accepted (recorded 2026-10-22; in force since the project began). Related: Why Julia, Parallelism and Compilation.

Context
Lenticulum’s workload is many small, heterogeneous factors, solvers inside differentiable programs, and query directions chosen at run time. A framework that traces a computation graph (PyTorch, JAX) handles that badly: graph breaks, recompilation for every new shape of query, and custom factors written in a second language.
Options

Julia.
An extension of PyTorch or JAX.
C++, Rust or Mojo.

Decision
Julia. In Julia ordinary code is the compiled, differentiable computation, so a user’s factor, belief type or solver loop needs no special treatment. Why Julia gives the full comparison and the costs.
Consequences

Lux.jl’s layer interface is the template for factors (L-SPEC-001 The Factor Interface).
RxInfer.jl and ModelingToolkit.jl are neighbours to interoperate with rather than reimplement (RxInfer as a Backend, ModelingToolkit as an Acausal Relation).
The costs listed in Why Julia §6 are accepted: compile latency, uneven AD across backends, type stability as the programmer’s job, and a smaller community.

Project/Decisions/L-ADR-0002-Energies-ar.filePath: Project/Decisions/L-ADR-0002 Energies are vectors, scalarised late.md
Project/Decisions/L-ADR-0002-Energies-ar.title: L-ADR-0002 Energies are vectors, scalarised late
Project/Decisions/L-ADR-0002-Energies-ar.content:
design

Status: accepted (recorded 2026-10-22; the design of Scalar and Multivariate Energy). Related: energy, statistical_game, L-ADR-0003 Pointwise energy and free energy are separate levels.

Context
AutoBayes gives a statistical game one non-negative scalar energy, and composites add them. Adding loses which factor contributed what, in which coordinates a factor is wrong, and the Jacobian of the residual. That rules out Gauss–Newton steps, the Fisher metric and the implicit function theorem, which Lenticulum’s implicit learners need.
Options

A scalar energy, as in the paper.
A vector energy in an energy space, with a scalarisation applied as late as possible.

Decision
Option 2: energies live in energy spaces, compose by direct sum, and a scalarisation turns them into a number. It was a requested design constraint (Scalar and Multivariate Energy, header).
Consequences

Linear scalarisations compose strictly; convex ones are lax, by a Jensen gap (§5 there), which islinear and jensen_gap expose.
The payoff, Jacobians of the vector energy, is not implemented yet: LP-002 The Jacobian side is not implemented.
Which scalarisation to use is a choice with consequences, listed in §8 there.

Project/Decisions/L-ADR-0003-Pointwise-e.filePath: Project/Decisions/L-ADR-0003 Pointwise energy and free energy are separate levels.md
Project/Decisions/L-ADR-0003-Pointwise-e.title: L-ADR-0003 Pointwise energy and free energy are separate levels
Project/Decisions/L-ADR-0003-Pointwise-e.content:
design

Status: accepted (2026-10-22, Daniel; merged to master in be229615). Related: Scalar and Multivariate Energy §7–§8, energy, GitHub issue #8, L-ADR-0002 Energies are vectors, scalarised late.

Context
A factor’s energyspace and scalarisation served both its pointwise energy (energy) and its free energy. For the residual factors they described only the free energy, graded (fit, complexity, negentropy). So scalar_energy applied a graded scalarisation to a residual vector and threw a MethodError (issue #8, reported by docxology).
Options

One space for both, as in AutoBayes: make the pointwise energy graded too, losing the residual vector.
Two levels, each with its own space and scalarisation, defaulting to one space.
Scalarisations as parameters chosen per call, like the p of a norm (Daniel’s direction), and per polarity.

Decision
Options 2 and 3 together. pointwise_energyspace and pointwise_scalarisation describe energy and default to energyspace and scalarisation. A residual factor’s pointwise energy is the signed residual with SquaredNorm(Q⁻¹). scalar_energy and scalar_free_energy take σ and polarity keywords. All four functions take an optional polarity, falling back to the polarity-free answer. Choices that fork the theory are documented, not fixed: Scalar and Multivariate Energy §8.
Consequences

At a point, the scalar pointwise energy equals the fit summand of the free energy; tested for four factors (test/runtests.jl, “pointwise energy and free energy: one contract”).
No factor depends on the polarity yet.
The free energy of a factor is built from the scalarised pointwise energy, not from the vector.

Project/Decisions/L-ADR-0004-The-vault-b.filePath: Project/Decisions/L-ADR-0004 The vault builds with the shared MathStruct Quartz.md
Project/Decisions/L-ADR-0004-The-vault-b.title: L-ADR-0004 The vault builds with the shared MathStruct Quartz
Project/Decisions/L-ADR-0004-The-vault-b.content:
design

Status: accepted (2026-10-21, Daniel; commit 5a850764). Related: MathStruct/quartz (its MATHSTRUCT.md), docs/site/build.sh, docs/site/README.md.

Context
Each MathStruct site carried its own copy of Quartz, and the copies had drifted: dark-mode TikZ, Markdown tabs and the wikilink fix each existed in only some of them. In this vault, tabs blocks rendered as raw source and about twenty wikilinks with code labels were broken.
Options

Keep a vendored Quartz per site.
One shared engine (MathStruct/quartz), with each site keeping only its configuration.
One site for all projects.

Decision
Option 2. docs/site/build.sh fetches MathStruct/quartz into docs/quartz, stages the vault and the implementation notes, and builds with docs/site/quartz.config.ts and quartz.layout.ts. QUARTZ_DIR points a build at a local checkout of the engine.
Consequences

A plugin or fix lands in MathStruct/quartz once and reaches this vault on its next build.
The vault’s rendering can change without a commit here; a build can be pinned with QUARTZ_REF.
docs/site/build.sh --serve previews the vault exactly as the website renders it.

Project/Decisions/L-ADR-0005-Branches.title: L-ADR-0005 Branches
Project/Decisions/L-ADR-0005-Branches.content:
design

Status: accepted (recorded 2026-10-22 from AGENTS.md, where it was already the rule). Related: AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/make.jl.

Context
The website publishes one branch, contributors need a place for pull requests, and the maintainer wants to see changes rendered before they are published.
Decision

master is what the site publishes: the vault at the root, the API docs under api/dev/.
dev is the shared branch where others’ work comes together, by pull request.
dev-danielb is the maintainer’s own branch. A push to it deploys a preview: the vault to preview/, the API docs to api/preview/. docs/make.jl chooses from the branch.
Work for the maintainer goes to dev-danielb; work for anyone else goes to a branch of its own, targeting dev. Nothing is merged to master unless the maintainer asks.

Consequences

A preview build has no comment threads (VAULT_COMMENTS=0), so discussions stay on the published pages.
An issue closed by a commit on dev-danielb closes only when the commit reaches master.

Project/Decisions/L-ADR-0006-Separate-li.title: L-ADR-0006 Separate likelihood_message from invert
Project/Decisions/L-ADR-0006-Separate-li.content:
design

Status: accepted (2026-10-24, Daniel: “keep both methods”; proposed 2026-10-23 on review-argon). Related: Messages are Inversions §5, lens, passing, gaussian §4, L-SPEC-001 The Factor Interface §2, §5.

Context
In AutoBayes (Definition 10), the Bayesian inversion c^\dagger_\pi(y) of a lens (c, c^\dagger) returns the posterior belief over the unobserved channel given the prior \pi and observation y: c^\dagger_\pi(y) \propto \pi \cdot \mu_{c\to\text{target}}(y). In belief propagation on a factor graph, however, the factor-to-variable message \mu_{c\to i} must be the likelihood contribution (with the cavity prior \pi divided out, using \pi at most as an expansion point for linearisation or Laplace approximation); otherwise a variable of degree d counts its prior d times.
Previously, Mycelium.factor_message’s generic fallback called LenticulumCore.invert(lens, prior, inputs, ps, st), while individual factors (ImplicitLayers, Adversarial, VariationalDiffusion) returned likelihoods from invert and Lenticulum’s GaussianFactor returned posteriors from invert and bypassed invert in factor_message.
Options

Have invert return the likelihood message everywhere, departing from AutoBayes Definition 10.
Have invert return the posterior everywhere and divide out the prior in Mycelium.factor_message via a belief division operation.
Add LenticulumCore.likelihood_message(lens, π, inputs, ps, st) -> (belief, st) for the cavity-free BP likelihood message (defaulting to invert(lens, π, inputs, ps, st) for lenses whose invert already returns a likelihood or point estimate), define invert on Gaussian/Laplace factors as combine(π, likelihood_message(...)), and have Mycelium.factor_message call likelihood_message.

Decision
Option 3. Belief division is ill-defined when the prior or message is improper or non-Gaussian (SampleBelief, DiracBelief), whereas forward multiplication (Mycelium.combine(π, msg)) is always well-defined. Separating likelihood_message (BP factor-to-variable likelihood) from invert (AutoBayes posterior) allows both contracts to hold without division or double-counting.
Consequences

LenticulumCore.invert(lens, π, inputs, ps, st) returns the posterior c^\dagger_\pi(y) = \pi \odot \mu_{c\to t} on GaussianFactor, LinearConstraintFactor, NonlinearFactor, and LikelihoodFactor.
LenticulumCore.likelihood_message(lens, π, inputs, ps, st) returns the likelihood message \mu_{c\to t}, using \pi only where needed as an expansion point (NonlinearFactor, LikelihoodFactor, DiffusionFactor).
Mycelium.factor_message’s generic fallback calls LenticulumCore.likelihood_message(lens, prior, inputs, ps, st).

Project/Problems/LP-001-The-vault-build-.filePath: Project/Problems/LP-001 The vault build uses GNU-only sed.md
Project/Problems/LP-001-The-vault-build-.title: LP-001 The vault build uses GNU-only sed
Project/Problems/LP-001-The-vault-build-.content:
open-problem

Status: closed (2026-10-23, review-argon; a CI guard added 2026-10-25, ba881303). Related: GitHub issue #9, docs/site/build.sh, L-ADR-0004 The vault builds with the shared MathStruct Quartz.

Problem. docs/site/build.sh substitutes the API address into the front page with sed -i "s#@API@#…#g" file. BSD sed (macOS) reads the expression as the backup suffix and fails, so the documented vault build does not run on a Mac (reported by docxology in issue #9).
Options.

sed -e … file > tmp && mv tmp file, which both seds accept.
Do the substitution in the shell, or write the front page with the address already in it.

Resolution. Option 1 implemented in docs/site/build.sh (sed -e ... "$STAGE/index.md" > "$STAGE/index.md.tmp" && mv "$STAGE/index.md.tmp" "$STAGE/index.md").
Follow-up (2026-10-25, Codex + Claude). docs/site/check_portability.py, run by the Docs workflow, fails on GNU-only shell forms and Bash 4 features in the docs tooling, so Linux CI now catches what issue #9 reported; @API@ is replaced literally, and a failed link rewrite stops the build.

Project/Problems/LP-002-The-Jacobian-sid.filePath: Project/Problems/LP-002 The Jacobian side is not implemented.md
Project/Problems/LP-002-The-Jacobian-sid.title: LP-002 The Jacobian side is not implemented
Project/Problems/LP-002-The-Jacobian-sid.content:
open-problem

Status: open (2026-10-22). Related: energy §“Implementation difficulties” 6, Scalar and Multivariate Energy §6, L-ADR-0002 Energies are vectors, scalarised late, Fisher information metric (CT-ML wiki).

Problem. The vector energy exists so that its Jacobian is available: Gauss–Newton steps, the Fisher metric of AutoBayes Definition 27, and the implicit function theorem. energy.jl provides the values and the algebra, but nothing extracts D_\theta \mathbf F. Until it does, the main payoff of L-ADR-0002 Energies are vectors, scalarised late is unrealised.
Options.

A Jacobian function in Lenticulum.jl proper, with one package extension per AD backend; LenticulumCore stays free of AD dependencies.
Per-factor hand-written Jacobians where a closed form exists (linear-Gaussian, constraint), AD elsewhere.

Leaning. Both: closed forms as tests, AD extensions as the general path. The compositional Fisher metric of Karwowski, Nielsen & Staton is a reference for how the pieces should combine.
Progress (review-argon, 2026-10-23). LenticulumCore now provides energy_jacobian(f, x, a, y, ps, st; wrt) (finite-difference reference on the pointwise vector energy) and gauss_newton_metric(f, x, a, y, ps, st; wrt) (J^\top M J for SquaredNorm(M)), keeping LenticulumCore free of AD dependencies. Parameter-space AD extensions (D_\theta \mathbf F) and closed-form factor overrides remain open.

Project/Problems/LP-003-SquaredNorm-does.filePath: Project/Problems/LP-003 SquaredNorm does not check its metric.md
Project/Problems/LP-003-SquaredNorm-does.title: LP-003 SquaredNorm does not check its metric
Project/Problems/LP-003-SquaredNorm-does.content:
open-problem

Status: closed (2026-10-25; first closed 2026-10-23 on review-argon, but that fix skipped structured matrices). Related: energy §“Implementation difficulties” 4, Scalar and Multivariate Energy §5.

Problem. SquaredNorm(M) computes \tfrac12 e^\top M e and assumes M symmetric positive semidefinite; nothing checks it. With an indefinite M the scalarisation is not convex, islinear still says false, and jensen_gap can be negative, which silently breaks the claim that the multivariate composite is a lower bound. energy calls it the sharpest outstanding correctness gap in the file.
Options.

Validate M at construction (a Cholesky attempt).
Store a factor L with M = L^\top L, so positive semidefiniteness holds by construction.
Document the precondition only (the current state).

Resolution. Option 1 implemented in lib/LenticulumCore.jl/src/energy.jl: SquaredNorm(M; check = true) verifies that M is square, symmetric, and positive semidefinite (attempting cholesky first for strictly PD matrices and falling back to eigvals for rank-deficient PSD matrices on standard float/integer strided matrices). Factors whose M = inv(Symmetric(f.Q)) is derived from an already-validated SPD Q pass check = false.
Reopened and closed again (2026-10-25, LP-013 Defects found in the review of master). The check ran only for StridedMatrix, so SquaredNorm(Diagonal([1, -1])) and its Symmetric form were accepted and returned -\tfrac12 at (0, 1). Now a Diagonal metric needs a real, nonnegative diagonal, and every other representation (symmetric, Hermitian, views) goes through the Cholesky/eigenvalue check (3254b1f8).

Project/Problems/LP-004-link_sources-rew.title: LP-004 link_sources rewrites unrelated notes
Project/Problems/LP-004-link_sources-rew.content:
open-problem

Status: closed (2026-10-23, review-argon). Related: AGENTS.md §“Citations”, docs/site/link_sources.py.

Problem. docs/site/link_sources.py adds the > Bibliography: line under each note’s sources. It also rewrites the Bibliography lines of a few unrelated notes (lib/VariationalDiffusion.jl/src/implicit.md, sampler.md, Backpropagation through Implicit Inference), dropping links that were there. Contributors are told to check git diff and restore those files by hand.
Options.

Find the matching rule that misfires (probably a citation key that is a prefix of another, or a source line it cannot parse) and fix it, with a test on the three notes.
Make the script refuse to remove an existing link, and report instead.

Resolution. Option 1 implemented in docs/site/link_sources.py: added unique (lead_author_lastname, year) matching anchored to the start of a citation clause ((?:^|[;:(]|\band)\s*), so Author Year and Author et al., Venue Year citations in implicit.md, sampler.md, and Backpropagation through Implicit Inference match directly without false co-author matches.
Trade-off (2026-10-24). The script now also keeps every existing > Bibliography: link whose key is still in refs.bib. That protects links it cannot re-derive, but a citation removed from a note’s sources keeps its link until the line is edited by hand. The new author–year matching anchors the lead author at the start of a citation clause, which avoids the false co-author match an earlier draft produced (Kingma, a co-author of Song et al. 2021, briefly gave The Diffusion Family a citation of Kingma et al. 2021).

Project/Problems/LP-005-Learning-the-noi.title: LP-005 Learning the noise covariance
Project/Problems/LP-005-Learning-the-noi.content:
open-problem

Status: open, later (2026-10-22). Related: src/gaussian.jl (GaussianFactor, GaussianPrior), Scalar and Multivariate Energy §8 (“Normalised or not”).

Problem. In GaussianFactor the noise covariance Q is a fixed hyperparameter, and GaussianPrior’s \Sigma is not learnable either: learning them needs a positive-definite parametrisation, which the code defers. It matters beyond convenience. The pointwise energy \tfrac12 r^\top Q^{-1} r leaves out the normaliser \tfrac12 \log\det(2\pi Q), a constant only while Q is fixed; once Q is learned, only the free energy, which keeps it as the complexity summand, is a valid objective.
Options.

A Cholesky factor with a log-diagonal, Q = L L^\top, as parameters.
A precision parametrisation, Q^{-1} = L L^\top, which is what the scalarisation uses.
Diagonal Q only, through log-variances.

Leaning. Not chosen. Whichever it is, training must use the free energy, and a test should show what goes wrong without it: the pointwise energy \tfrac12 r^\top Q^{-1} r alone decreases as Q grows, so it drives Q \to \infty (variance inflation); the normaliser \tfrac12 \log\det(2\pi Q) in the free energy penalises that. At an exact fit (r = 0) the likelihood is unbounded as Q \to 0, so even the free energy needs a prior on Q or a floor. (Direction corrected 2026-10-25; it said Q \to 0.)

Project/Problems/LP-006-Gaussian-entropi.filePath: Project/Problems/LP-006 Gaussian entropies are relative to Lebesgue measure.md
Project/Problems/LP-006-Gaussian-entropi.title: LP-006 Gaussian entropies are relative to Lebesgue measure
Project/Problems/LP-006-Gaussian-entropi.content:
open-problem

Status: accepted, documented (2026-10-22). Related: Scalar and Multivariate Energy §8, Entropy in a Markov Category (CT-ML wiki), Bethe Free Energy.

Problem. The free energies of the Gaussian factors use differential entropies, e.g. \tfrac12\log\det(2\pi e \Sigma). In Perrone’s categorical account the KL entropy of a probability measure is Shannon entropy if it is discrete and infinite otherwise (Markov Categories and Entropy, Corollary 4.7): copying a continuous variable gives a measure on the diagonal, singular with respect to p \otimes p. Differential entropy is finite only because it is taken relative to Lebesgue measure, and it changes under reparametrisation.
Resolution. Accepted: free energies of continuous beliefs are relative to a reference measure, Lebesgue in the coordinates of each variable. Consequences to keep in mind:

free energies are comparable between models over the same coordinates, not across reparametrisations;
a change of variables inside a factor must add its log-Jacobian;
mixing discrete and continuous variables in one free energy needs care with the reference measures.

Project/Problems/LP-007-Missing-implemen.title: LP-007 Missing implementation notes
Project/Problems/LP-007-Missing-implemen.content:
open-problem

Status: closed (2026-10-23, review-argon). Related: Start Here §“Adding to it”, Map of Content §4.

Problem. Every Julia file is meant to have an implementation note beside it. src/gaussian.jl and src/beliefs.jl have none (gaussian.md, beliefs.md), although their docstrings cite beliefs.md, gaussian.md (§2, §3) and a vault note The Gaussian Factor, which does not exist either. Those references point nowhere; src/constraint.md already flags this.
Resolution. Wrote src/gaussian.md and src/beliefs.md covering the theory, implementation, what they do not do (LP-005), and implementation difficulties, and updated src/gaussian.jl to reference Scalar and Multivariate Energy.md.

Project/Problems/LP-008-No-conformance-t.filePath: Project/Problems/LP-008 No conformance test for the factor interface.md
Project/Problems/LP-008-No-conformance-t.title: LP-008 No conformance test for the factor interface
Project/Problems/LP-008-No-conformance-t.content:
open-problem

Status: open, partly addressed (2026-10-25). The 2026-10-23 resolution named a function that did not exist. Related: L-SPEC-001 The Factor Interface, GitHub issue #8.

Problem. The factor interface is tested factor by factor. Issue #8 was a mismatch between two parts of the contract (scalarisation and energy) that no test covered, because each factor’s tests exercised only the paths it used. Other factor types (the diffusion, equilibrium, neural-ODE and adversarial factors) may have similar gaps.
Options.

A conformance test: a function check_factor(f, ps, st, samples) in a test utility that runs every applicable part of L-SPEC-001 The Factor Interface (§1–§5) and the consistency conditions between them, called from each package’s tests for each factor type.
Keep per-factor tests and add the cross-checks by hand.

Resolution so far. The review-argon commits claimed option 1 (check_factor_conformance) but only added a loop over traits; the function did not exist (LP-013 Defects found in the review of master). Since bb3af9e9 it does, in test/factor_conformance.jl: for a factor and polarity it checks the testable parts of L-SPEC-001 The Factor Interface §1–§5 (traits, invert = combine(π, likelihood_message), the pointwise energy and its scalarisation, game-level free_energy and entropy in energyspace). It runs over every supported polarity of GaussianFactor, GaussianPrior, LinearConstraintFactor, NonlinearFactor and LikelihoodFactor (297 checks). Open: the factors of Mycelium, ImplicitLayers, VariationalDiffusion and Adversarial are not run through it yet.

Project/Problems/LP-009-Game-level-free-.filePath: Project/Problems/LP-009 Game-level free energy is declared but not implemented.md
Project/Problems/LP-009-Game-level-free-.title: LP-009 Game-level free energy is declared but not implemented
Project/Problems/LP-009-Game-level-free-.content:
open-problem

Status: open, partly addressed (2026-10-25). The 2026-10-23 resolution listed methods that do not exist. Related: L-SPEC-001 The Factor Interface §4–§5, statistical_game, abstract_types, factors.

Problem. LenticulumCore declares the game-level entropy(f, π, y, ps, st) and free_energy(f, π, y, ps, st) (AutoBayes Definition 20), and abstract_types.jl lists entropy among the methods a factor must provide. No factor implements either. Every factor that is used in a graph implements Mycelium’s local_free_energy(f, msgs, ps, st) instead, which takes all incoming messages because a graph has no distinguished prior/observation split. So scalar_free_energy(f, π, y, ...) fails for every factor in the repository, the same kind of gap as issue #8.
Options.

Derive the game-level free energy from local_free_energy, by passing the prior as the message on the unobserved channel and a Dirac belief on the observed one.
Implement free_energy and entropy per factor.
Drop them from the required list, and document local_free_energy as the free energy of a factor.

Resolution so far. Option 1 for the five Lenticulum factors (GaussianFactor, GaussianPrior, LinearConstraintFactor, NonlinearFactor, LikelihoodFactor): free_energy passes the prior and the observation to Mycelium.local_free_energy, and since 4a49ca5c entropy returns an element of the energy space, not a bare number. PriorFactor has exact game-level methods for Dirac and categorical beliefs (bb3af9e9); for a Gaussian belief with an arbitrary nlogp they throw, because the expectation has no closed form. The 2026-10-23 resolution also listed a generic LenticulumCore fallback and methods for EqualityFactor, DeterministicFactor, the equilibrium and neural-ODE factors; none of these exist (LP-013 Defects found in the review of master). Open: those factors. The DEQ and neural-ODE factors solve for a point, so an exact distributional free energy needs a choice (a Dirac belief, or a stated approximation).

Project/Problems/LP-010-Where-the-graph-.filePath: Project/Problems/LP-010 Where the graph of a problem comes from.md
Project/Problems/LP-010-Where-the-graph-.title: LP-010 Where the graph of a problem comes from
Project/Problems/LP-010-Where-the-graph-.content:
open-problem

Status: open, theory (2026-10-22, Daniel: “How do we actually find out the graph for a problem? That looks to me a lot like topological data analysis. And should be done before.”). Related: Dynamic Graphs §4, Bethe Free Energy, Loopy Message Passing, Motivating Examples, ModelingToolkit as an Acausal Relation, RxInfer as a Backend.

Problem. Everything in the vault starts from a given factor graph. For a new problem, someone has to find it first: which variables exist, which of them interact, and through which factors. The vault does not say how.
Routes, from most to least prior knowledge.

From a model. Equations (ModelingToolkit) or a probabilistic program (an RxInfer @model) already are the graph; most of the Motivating Examples are of this kind (circuits, SLAM, power grids).
Structure learning from data. Which variables depend on which: conditional-independence tests (the PC algorithm), score-based search (GES, NOTEARS), the graphical lasso for Gaussian models. Lenticulum’s own score is already designed: the Bethe criterion of Dynamic Graphs §4 compares the free energy with and without a candidate factor, which is score-based structure search one factor at a time.
Topological data analysis. Mapper draws a graph of the data’s shape, and persistent homology finds its clusters and loops. A Mapper graph’s nodes are regions of the data, not variables, so it is not a factor graph. TDA is exploration before route 2: which regimes exist, whether one graph fits all of them. It also applies to a factor graph itself, whose cycles decide where loopy message passing is only approximate (Loopy Message Passing).

Observation. Lenticulum has a fourth route the others lack: learn one relation over the joint space (a diffusion factor over all variables), then split it. Splitting a joint factor into smaller ones whose product approximates it is structure learning by factorisation, and the free energy measures what the split costs. This is an expectation, not something the code does.
Leaning. “Should be done before” is right as an order: explore (TDA) → propose a structure (model, or structure learning) → fit (Lenticulum) → revise with the Bethe criterion. A note in Factor Graphs/ on this pipeline, with one worked example, is the next step. Moonkale’s part would be showing each step’s result as a graph to accept or edit.

Project/Problems/LP-011-Gradient-couplin.filePath: Project/Problems/LP-011 Gradient couplings and isfrozen are declared but unused.md
Project/Problems/LP-011-Gradient-couplin.title: LP-011 Gradient couplings and isfrozen are declared but unused
Project/Problems/LP-011-Gradient-couplin.content:
open-problem

Status: open (2026-10-22). Related: L-SPEC-002 Stop Gradient, Factors are Parameterized Statistical Games, The Type Discipline of a Factor Graph §4. Code: abstract_types.jl, statistical_game.jl, lib/Mycelium.jl/src/graph.jl.

Problem. The design says the choice of gradient coupling is made per edge (connect!(…; coupling = DiagonalCoupling()), ComposedFactor(…; coupling)), and that a frozen factor (isfrozen) differs from a non-learnable one in the backward pass. Both are stored or declared, and no code reads them: a search for uses of the coupling field or isfrozen finds only their definitions. So a user who sets coupling = ScoreFunctionCoupling() gets no error and no effect.
Options.

Implement them as part of the graph-level backward pass (Backward Signatures) and the stop-gradient specification.
Until then, warn (or throw) when a non-default coupling is set, so the setting is not silently ignored.

Leaning. Option 2 now, option 1 with L-SPEC-002 Stop Gradient.

Project/Problems/LP-012-Factor-graphs-an.title: LP-012 Factor graphs and schemes
Project/Problems/LP-012-Factor-graphs-an.content:
open-problem

Status: open, theory (2026-10-22, Daniel: “Also is there a connection to schemes from algebraic geometry? I do not know much about that.”). Related: Algebraic Statistics Bridge, Varieties Ideals and Real Nullstellensatz, Branches and the Discriminant, Composition is Elimination, Bethe Free Energy.

Question. Is there a connection between Lenticulum’s factor graphs and schemes?
What is already in the vault. Algebraic Statistics Bridge shows that conditional independence is a polynomial (determinantal) constraint, so a discrete or Gaussian graphical model is an algebraic variety, and marginalisation is elimination. Schemes generalise varieties, so the question is what the generalisation adds. Three candidate links, none worked out here:

Singular models. Where a model’s variety is singular, parameters are not identifiable and the Fisher metric degenerates; that is where model selection gets hard. Watanabe’s singular learning theory (Algebraic Geometry and Statistical Learning Theory, 2009) handles this with resolution of singularities, and the real log canonical threshold replaces the parameter count in the evidence. Lenticulum’s evidence and Bethe-criterion comparisons (Dynamic Graphs §4) would meet exactly this when learned factors are overparametrised.
Tangent vectors are dual-number points. In scheme language the tangent space of X at a point is the set of maps \mathrm{Spec}\,\mathbb R[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2) \to X: solutions of the defining equations over the dual numbers. That is forward-mode automatic differentiation, and the “jets” of the CT-ML wiki’s Information Geometry of Probabilistic Programs. Schemes keep this first-order information even where the variety is singular, which is where the Fisher metric of Scalar and Multivariate Energy §6 is degenerate.
Sheaves. A scheme is built by gluing local pieces with a sheaf of functions. A factor graph can be read as a cellular sheaf: every variable and factor carries a space of local states, every edge a map saying how they must agree; global sections are the consistent assignments, and the sheaf Laplacian measures inconsistency (Hansen & Ghrist, Toward a spectral theory of cellular sheaves, 2019). Message passing would then be a way to compute (approximate) global sections. Sheaves are the ingredient factor graphs and schemes share.

Leaning. Link 3 is the closest to the code and would give the CT-ML wiki a Cellular Sheaf note; link 1 is the one with consequences for model selection. Both need reading before a vault note; the references above are to be checked and added to refs.bib first.

Project/Problems/LP-013-Defects-found-in.filePath: Project/Problems/LP-013 Defects found in the review of master.md
Project/Problems/LP-013-Defects-found-in.title: LP-013 Defects found in the review of master
Project/Problems/LP-013-Defects-found-in.content:
open-problem

Status: closed (2026-10-25). Related: L-SPEC-001 The Factor Interface, L-ADR-0006 Separate likelihood_message from invert, LP-003 SquaredNorm does not check its metric, LP-008 No conformance test for the factor interface, LP-009 Game-level free energy is declared but not implemented.

Problem. A read-only review of master by Codex (2026-10-25, of the 16 commits after 5a850764: the issue #8 energy work, the cherry-picked review-argon fixes, L-ADR-0006) found defects that the test suites passed over, each with a reproduction. Besides reopening LP-003, LP-008 and LP-009:

entropy returned a bare number for the five Lenticulum factors, though its contract makes it an element of the energy space; applying the factor’s own GradedScalarisation to it threw a MethodError.
The nonlinear factor’s likelihood_message and invert disagreed for iterations > 1: only invert relinearised at the posterior, so the BP message was not the site of the posterior (against L-ADR-0006). For f(x) = x^2, noise 0.1, prior \mathcal N(1, 1), y = 4, four iterations: posterior mean 1.9938 from invert, 2.4634 from the prior times the message.
Predictive LikelihoodFactor free energy set fit and the conditional entropy both to 0, because they cancel in the plain sum; any other scalarisation got the wrong value (ordinal, thresholds \pm1, x = 0: both are 0.8448).
The mixture likelihood_message (VariationalDiffusion) kept the posterior’s weights after dividing out the anchor; the weights also need each component’s log-partition change (two modes, anchor \mathcal N(0.4, 4): weights 0.68/0.32 against 0.59/0.41).
The prior’s cotangent in implicit_factor_pullback was the first unobserved block’s cotangent even when an incoming point overrode the prior: 0.20 where finite differences give 0.
RQ-002 and Universal Approximation for Implicit Diffusion Learners §3 claimed an O((\sigma^\ast)^2) error from uniform continuity alone; uncentred shifts give O(\sigma^\ast).

Resolution. Codex implemented the fixes test-first on codex/review-fixes, one commit each; Claude reviewed them, kept predictive mode working for the count likelihoods (Codex had made it throw) by summing their conditional entropy as a series, and corrected the notes: 1 → 4a49ca5c; 2 → c03014c3, with the graph message on the same routine in bb3af9e9; 3 → c5f07b5a, 3be38b3e; 4 → 4c184538; 5 → 84b69146; 6 → the notes now say o(1), O(\sigma^\ast) for \hat G \in C^3, and O((\sigma^\ast)^2) only for centred shifts and \hat G \in C^4. The review is Lenticulum.jl-Review/10_Review_of_master_(Codex).md (outside the repository).
Lesson. Records were marked closed on the strength of commit messages. A resolution names the code or test that closes it, and is checked against the code before the status changes.

Project/Specifications/L-SPEC-001-The-Fa.title: L-SPEC-001 The Factor Interface

Project/Specifications/L-SPEC-002-Stop-G.title: L-SPEC-002 Stop Gradient
Project/Specifications/L-SPEC-002-Stop-G.content:
design

Status: planned (2026-10-22, Daniel: “one spec for later would be stop gradient. That seems kinda important”). Related: L-SPEC-001 The Factor Interface, Factors are Parameterized Statistical Games §“Parameters, and the gradient the paper asks for”, Backward Signatures, RED-Diff as a Statistical Game §3, LP-011 Gradient couplings and isfrozen are declared but unused. Code: lib/LenticulumCore.jl/src/abstract_types.jl (AbstractGradientCoupling), statistical_game.jl (isfrozen), lib/Mycelium.jl/src/graph.jl (EdgeDirection, connect!).

Scope
A stop gradient lets values pass forward but no gradient flow back: JAX’s stop_gradient, PyTorch’s detach, ChainRulesCore.ignore_derivatives in Julia. In Lenticulum there are several things one could mean by it, and the repository already has a piece of each. This specification is to say which ones are part of the interface, how a user asks for them, and what the backward pass then computes. It is not written yet; this note records the scope.
What exists



































meaningwherestateDetach a value. No cotangent crosses a wire (frozen targets, EM-style alternation, straight-through estimators)nothing Lenticulum-specific; ignore_derivatives works inside a factor’s own code—Freeze parameters. A factor’s ps are not updated, but cotangents still flow through it to upstream factorsisfrozen(factor); its docstring warns that confusing it with islearnable “silently detaches a subgraph”declared, never consultedDrop coupling terms. Keep only the block-diagonal of the composite Jacobian (AutoBayes Definition 29): stop the gradient through the sampling path and the pushforward priorDiagonalCoupling() per edge (connect!(…; coupling)), the default; alternatives PathwiseCoupling, ScoreFunctionCoupling, ExactCouplingstored on edges, never readOne-way messages. A wire carries messages in one direction only (the message-passing analogue)Emitting(), Absorbing() edge directionsimplemented: the schedules prune forbidden messagesA stop-gradient as the method. RED-Diff’s regulariser gradient treats the network output as constantRED-Diff as a Statistical Game §3; Implicit Diffusion Learners proves the resulting field conservativeimplemented in VariationalDiffusion.jl
Open (for the specification)

Per wire, per factor, or per parameter subset? Stopping with respect to some parameters only (stop the gradient into the encoder, not the decoder) is the common case in amortised inference.
How it composes with the Backward Signatures design: a stopped wire returns NoTangent() in the factor-level rrule; a frozen factor still returns input cotangents.
Whether DiagonalCoupling should stay the default once couplings are read: it is the cheapest choice and also a biased one.
Whether a straight-through estimator (custom backward pass) belongs here or is a separate factor.
One rule per meaning, a test per rule, and how ADEV-style estimators (the CT-ML wiki’s Automatic Differentiation of Expected Values) supply the dropped coupling terms.

Project/Specifications/L-SPEC-003-Expose.filePath: Project/Specifications/L-SPEC-003 Exposed Parameters and Energy Channels.md
Project/Specifications/L-SPEC-003-Expose.title: L-SPEC-003 Exposed Parameters and Energy Channels
Project/Specifications/L-SPEC-003-Expose.content:
design

Status: planned (2026-10-25, Daniel: “If the library is extensible in this direction one should plan for it”). Related: Unusual Wirings (the theory), L-SPEC-001 The Factor Interface, L-SPEC-002 Stop Gradient, Everything is a Factor, The Inferencer and the Optimizer §7, RQ-007 Risk Scalarisations and Local Decomposition, LP-005 Learning the noise covariance. Code: lib/LenticulumCore.jl/src/channels.jl, energy.jl, statistical_game.jl; lib/Mycelium.jl/src/factors.jl (OptimiserFactor, PriorFactor), graph.jl, free_energy.jl.

Scope
Three extensions of L-SPEC-001 The Factor Interface that let a graph wire an output into a
weight, an energy into an input, and keep beliefs over weights and energies (Unusual Wirings).
None is built. This note records the intended shape, so that work on the existing interface does
not close the door on them; the contract below is a proposal, and each part becomes binding only
when it is implemented with its tests.
Today





























capabilitystatea parameter as a variableonly by writing a factor whose weight is a channel; OptimiserFactor and PriorFactor then attach to it. No generic way to expose a block of pssharing a weight between factorsno tying interface: ps is per factor (The Inferencer and the Optimizer §7.1); two entries can alias one array, but shared gradients and updates are not handledan energy as a value another factor readsno generic tap: a custom factor can call energy/scalar_energy of another, but no wiring exposes an existing factor’s energy as a channela belief over an energyno standard API: factors return evaluated, expected or estimated quantities (Gaussian fit is an expectation, DEQ energies are evaluated at points, the diffusion factor’s score term is Monte Carlo), never the distributionscalarisation of an energy beliefno: scalarise(σ, e) takes a value in an energy space
The proposed contract
§1 Exposure. expose(f, names::Tuple) returns a factor whose channels are channels(f) plus
one channel per parameter block in names (its space the block’s shape), and whose ps lack those
blocks.

§1.1 With every exposed channel hard-clamped (a DiracBelief), it behaves exactly as f with those blocks
substituted: messages, energies and free energies are f’s. (Testable against f for every
factor; this part needs nothing from f.) An observed channel with finite precision is an
uncertain weight and falls under §1.2.
§1.2 With an exposed channel unobserved, the factor needs the message to that channel. A
factor provides it by an optional method parameter_message(f, name, polarity, msgs, ps, st), which
returns a likelihood message (the prior on the weight is a separate factor, as for any variable,
L-ADR-0006 Separate likelihood_message from invert); for the linear-Gaussian factor in A with a
point x it is an exact, possibly improper, Gaussian kernel (the factor is linear in A). Without the method,
a generic Laplace message by AD may be used, and its docstring and the polarity say it is an
approximation. Beliefs on both x and A make the factor bilinear: mean-field (VMP) or EP, stated.
§1.3 Two exposed channels connected to one variable share the weight; this replaces
name-keyed ps for weight tying.

§2 Energy taps. tap(f) returns a factor with an extra channel :energy in
pointwise_energyspace(f).

§2.1 Unobserved: the message is the energy’s pushforward under the factor belief; exact for a
Dirac belief, otherwise by samples or a stated approximation.
§2.2 Observed with finite precision \tau: the tap owns a quadratic penalty \tfrac\tau2\lVert E_f - e\rVert^2, a
term of its own in the free energy beside f‘s; with infinite precision, a level-set constraint,
supported only where a disintegration is available (as for LinearConstraintFactor), whose
reference measure and entropy treatment the implementation must state.
§2.3 Gradients: by default no cotangent flows back through :energy into f (a stop-gradient,
L-SPEC-002 Stop Gradient); a user may switch it on.
§2.4 Bethe accounting: the tap contributes f’s free-energy term once, plus §2.2’s penalty when
:energy is observed. A factor that reads :energy adds its own term; the sum must not contain
E_f twice unless the reader says it reweights it. That an unobserved, unread tap leaves the Bethe
free energy unchanged is a property to prove (the deterministic e = E_f(x) makes the joint
singular with respect to Lebesgue measure, so the entropy convention matters), and to test.

§3 Energy beliefs and risk scalarisations.

§3.1 Two different objects, not to be conflated: the pushforward of the factor belief under
the pointwise energy (a belief over pointwise_energyspace(f), e.g. the residual r, whose mean is
not fit: for r \sim \mathcal N(0, 1), \mathbb E r = 0 but fit = \tfrac12), and the law of the scalar loss whose
expectation is a free-energy coordinate (e.g. \tfrac12 r^\top Q^{-1} r, mean fit). Entropy coordinates
are functionals of the belief, not means of a random energy, and have no such law. An optional
energy_belief(f, msgs, ps, st) returns the first; risk scalarisations act on the second.
§3.2 Scalarisations that act on such a belief: Expectation() (today’s semantics),
EntropicRisk(β), CVaR(α). Each documents when it is finite (the entropic risk needs a finite
positive exponential moment, which an energy with a heavier-than-exponential right tail lacks) and how it composes over factors
(RQ-007 Risk Scalarisations and Local Decomposition).

Keep open meanwhile
Changes to the current interface should not make these harder:

a Channel’s space may be matrix-valued or an energy space, not only a vector length;
scalarise stays a generic function that can gain methods on beliefs;
Mycelium does not assume parameters and variables are disjoint kinds (an OptimiserFactor
already attaches to a variable that is a parameter);
local_free_energy keeps returning coordinates that are expectations of named terms, so that
§3.1 can return their distribution without changing their meaning.

Checked by
Nothing yet. The first tests: §1.1 against the unexposed factor for every factor in the conformance
checker (test/factor_conformance.jl); §1.2 for the linear-Gaussian factor in A against the
closed-form posterior of a Bayesian linear regression; §2.4 by a Bethe sum with a tap, compared
with the sum without it; §3.2 against closed forms for Gaussian energies (entropic risk of
\mathcal N(m, s^2) is m + \beta s^2/2).
Open

Whether exposure is a wrapper (expose(f, …)) or a property each factor declares.
How exposed weights meet LuxCore’s parameter handling and Optimisers.jl setups.
Whether energy taps need §2.3’s stop-gradient to be a per-wire option, which depends on
L-SPEC-002 Stop Gradient.
Which risk scalarisations admit message passing: RQ-007 Risk Scalarisations and Local Decomposition.

Project/Specifications/L-SPEC-004-Algebr.filePath: Project/Specifications/L-SPEC-004 Algebraic Factors Toric and Grassmannian.md
Project/Specifications/L-SPEC-004-Algebr.title: L-SPEC-004 Algebraic Factors Toric and Grassmannian
Project/Specifications/L-SPEC-004-Algebr.content:
design

Status: planned (2026-10-25, Daniel: “Could you plan for that?”, on Gemini’s suggestion to start the algebraic family with the easier and useful cases, toric varieties and the Grassmannian). Related: Toric Models as Factors, Grassmann Mixing and Plücker Coordinates, The Parameter is a Grassmannian, Algebraic Implicit Learners, Open Problems in Algebraic Implicit Learning, L-SPEC-001 The Factor Interface, L-SPEC-003 Exposed Parameters and Energy Channels. Code: none yet; it would touch lib/Mycelium.jl/src/factors.jl (update rules), messages.jl (categorical beliefs), free_energy.jl.

Scope
The first code for the algebraic family, whose sixteen notes (Algebraic Implicit Learners)
have no implementation. Gemini’s review (Proposal 7 of 05_Architectural_Design_Proposals.md in
the review folder) sketches a whole package lib/AlgebraicFactors.jl; this specification orders
it so that the cases where everything is exact or cheap come first:

toric factors (Toric Models as Factors): exact discrete factors with known implicit
equations;
Grassmannian parameters (The Parameter is a Grassmannian): projection and retraction for
parameters defined up to a gauge;
the general polynomial factor, on top of both;
multi-branch inference by homotopy continuation, last.

Plücker coordinates (Grassmann Mixing and Plücker Coordinates) enter as a small
deterministic factor and as test data. The contract below is a proposal; each part becomes
binding when it is implemented with its tests.
Today

























capabilitystatea factor over several discrete variablesnone. Categorical beliefs exist and combine (messages.jl), PriorFactor takes one, LikelihoodFactor predicts one; no factor sums a table over several channelsparameters on a manifoldnone. Mycelium’s update rules (GradientDescent, Momentum, Nesterov through rule_get/rule_put) are Euclideana polynomial (Veronese) factor, nullspace fittingnone; the theory is in the notesmulti-branch rootsnone; MixtureBelief exists to carry them
The proposed contract
§0 Package. lib/AlgebraicFactors.jl, depending on LenticulumCore, Mycelium and
LinearAlgebra only, until §4 adds a package extension. Tests and docs are wired like the other
packages under lib/.
§1 Toric factors.

§1.1 ToricFactor(names::Tuple, alphabets::Tuple, A::AbstractMatrix{<:Integer}; normalised = false):
one channel per name, of the alphabet’s size. The joint states are ordered column-major over the
alphabets (documented), and column x of A is a_x; the constructor checks
size(A, 2) == prod(alphabets). Constructors build A for common cases:
independence(names, alphabets) and hierarchical(names, alphabets, generators)
(marginal-cell indicators per generator).
§1.2 Parameters ps = (η = …,) in \mathbb R^d. p_\eta = p_{\eta'} iff A^\top(\eta-\eta') \in \operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1\} (the docstring
says so); an optional reduction to independent logit differences is a chart, not a change of
model. Statements that need \mathbf 1 in the row space of A use \bar A = \binom{\mathbf 1^\top}{A} internally
(Toric Models as Factors).
§1.3 energy(f, x, …) is -\langle\eta, a_x\rangle, plus \Lambda(\eta) when normalised; x is a tuple of labels. Scalar.
§1.4 factor_message(f, target, polarity, inputs, prior, ps, st) -> (belief, st): the exact
sum-product likelihood message to target, a CategoricalBelief. Observed inputs may be Diracs
on labels or categorical beliefs; latent channels (missing or uninformative inputs, which
Mycelium resolves to Latent()) are summed over with unit weight, so ordinary BP initialisation
works. The message excludes the target’s prior. The cost, \prod alphabets per message, is stated.
§1.5 local_free_energy(f, msgs, ps, st): \mathbb E_{b_f}E - H(b_f) for the factor belief
b_f \propto \psi_\eta \prod_u \mu_{u\to f}, exact, in the form PriorFactor returns it (a scalar). With
normalised = true, the game-level free_energy and entropy of L-SPEC-001 The Factor Interface §4
are exact as well.
§1.6 fit_mle(f, counts; method = :newton | :ipf), returning \eta, a convergence status and,
separately, an existence status. The stopping test is moment matching, \lVert A\hat p - Au/n\rVert
(Birch), which can also approach zero at an extended MLE on the boundary. Without an existence
certificate (§Open), a diverging \eta is reported as non-convergence or suspected boundary
convergence, never as proven non-existence, and never silently. Newton removes the gauge
directions first.
§1.7 inmodel(f, p; atol): for positive p, whether \log p lies in the row space of \bar A (least
squares). binomial_residuals(f, p, moves) evaluates p^{u^+} - p^{u^-} for moves the user supplies.
No Markov-basis computation.

§2 Grassmannian parameters.

§2.1 Grassmann(k, m), represented by \Theta \in \mathbb R^{k\times m} with \Theta\Theta^\top = I_k:
project_tangent(M, Θ, G) = G - G\Theta^\top\Theta; retract(M, Θ, Δ) orthonormalises the rows of
\Theta + \Delta by a thin QR of the transpose, with signs chosen so that \operatorname{diag}(R) > 0, so that
R_\Theta(0) = \Theta (in exact arithmetic; tested with ≈); rand(rng, M). (Edelman, Arias & Smith 1998; Absil, Mahony & Sepulchre 2008.)
§2.2 Retracted(rule, M) <: AbstractUpdateRule for Mycelium’s optimiser lens, at first for
GradientDescent and Momentum only, with rule_get(...) = Θ. rule_put projects the gradient,
applies rule, converts the candidate point it returns into a displacement p' - \Theta, projects
that onto the tangent space and retracts. A rule’s state (momentum) is projected onto the new
tangent space, which is a vector transport for an embedded manifold (Absil, Mahony & Sepulchre
2008). Nesterov waits: its look-ahead p + \gamma s leaves the manifold, and a retracted look-ahead
with a consistent transport of the gradient has to be specified first. This is the lens G^*(\Theta, \Delta) = \mathrm{qf}(\Theta + \Pi_\Theta\Delta) of
The Parameter is a Grassmannian.
§2.3 Gauge invariance as a test obligation: a factor whose relation depends on \Theta only
through its row space must give the same scalarised energy for \Theta and B\Theta (B invertible)
under its default scalarisation. The Sampson energy \tfrac12 r^\top(JJ^\top)^{-1}r with J = D_z r_\Theta of full row
rank has this property (Algebraic versus Geometric Distance), but today’s scalarisations see
only the residual, not J; a point- and parameter-dependent scalarisation has to be specified
first, with its behaviour at singular points (damping or a pseudoinverse does not keep the
invariance by itself). Checked once §3 exists.
§2.4 With L-SPEC-003 Exposed Parameters and Energy Channels, an exposed Grassmannian
parameter is a channel whose space is a manifold; that spec’s “keep open” list already allows it.

§3 The polynomial factor (after §1 and §2), as in Gemini’s Proposal 7: an exponent table with
monomial or Chebyshev basis, the residual r_\Theta(z) = \Theta v_d(z) as the pointwise energy, the
Sampson scalarisation (after the interface of §2.3), fit_nullspace and Sampson IRLS (Fitting is a Nullspace Problem),
and single-branch messages by Newton with a Laplace Gaussian
(Inference as Root Finding).
§4 Multi-branch inference (last): a HomotopyContinuation.jl package extension finding all
isolated real roots and returning a MixtureBelief over branches
(Branches and the Discriminant).
§5 Plücker. plucker(z, w) and its Jacobian; a deterministic PluckerFactor(r) with the
forward polarity only (the inverse message would be a belief on an SL_2-orbit, not built); and
plucker_relations(r), the quadrics p_{ij}p_{kl} - p_{ik}p_{jl} + p_{il}p_{jk}, as test data.
Checked by
Nothing yet. The first tests:

§1: the independence model, whose MLE is the outer product of the margins; the chain
A - B - C as a decomposable model with positive margins, against \hat p_{AB}\hat p_{BC}/\hat p_B; belief propagation on a
tree of ToricFactors against enumeration of the joint (marginals and \log Z); the gradient
Au/n - Ap_\eta against finite differences; Newton against IPF; inmodel true at a fit and false
at a generic p; for a table with an empty row, a status that is not “converged”, and the
extended MLE (the outer product of the margins) as the limit; the conformance checker
(test/factor_conformance.jl) over every supported polarity, which today calls assemble,
invert and likelihood_message: either ToricFactor implements the lens methods, or the checker
is extended to direct-message factors with equivalent checks.
§2: \Theta\Theta^\top = I after retract; project_tangent(M, Θ, G) * Θ' ≈ 0; retract(M, Θ, zero(Θ)) ≈ Θ;
for symmetric S with \lambda_k < \lambda_{k+1}, generic initialisation and a suitable step rule, Riemannian
descent on \operatorname{tr}(\Theta S\Theta^\top) reaching the span of the k smallest eigenvectors (the nullspace fit’s
answer), compared by principal angles and by the objective against \sum_{i\le k}\lambda_i.
§3 with §5: on points z\wedge w for random z, w \in \mathbb R^4, fit_nullspace of degree 2 should
recover the Klein quadric, a one-dimensional null space, with at least 27 generic points and
a stated rank tolerance (an expectation, agreeing with a scratch check;
Grassmann Mixing and Plücker Coordinates).

Open

MLE existence: deciding whether Au/n lies in the relative interior of the convex hull of the
columns of \bar A (Fienberg & Rinaldo 2012) needs a linear program; whether to depend on an LP solver.
Markov bases need external software (4ti2 and similar); whether to depend on it.
Large tables: messages are exponential in arity. Whether hierarchical should split into one
factor per generator automatically is a junction-tree question
(LP-010 Where the graph of a problem comes from).
Beliefs on the Grassmannian (rather than points on it) are not planned.
A causal Grassmann-mixing block (Grassmann Mixing and Plücker Coordinates §“What Lenticulum
can take”) is an experiment for LenticulumLM, not part of this package.
